Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 2-day history of mid-lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain with mild nausea, low-grade temperature (37 °C), increased urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine. No dysuria, no flank pain, no significant systemic features.  
• Most consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower urinary tract infection). DDx system ranks this “High” likelihood and aligns with clinical presentation.  
• Alternative considerations (DDx): distal urolithiasis (Medium likelihood) given hematuria and abdominal discomfort; early appendicitis (Low-Medium) considered but urinary findings make this less likely.  
• No evidence of pyelonephritis (no flank pain/fever) or pelvic inflammatory disease (no vaginal symptoms).  
• Plan: empiric 3-day oral antibiotic course (twice daily; specific drug not documented) sent to nominated pharmacy; safety-net advice provided (seek review if pain worsens, fever develops, back pain, or recurrence).  
• Allergy: amoxicillin—antibiotic choice should avoid penicillins.  
• Pregnancy not specifically ruled out; consider urine β-hCG if symptoms persist (not ordered).  

Management Plan
- 3-day course of oral antibiotic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) to start as soon as dispensed.  
- Hydration advice; monitor symptoms.  
- Safety-net: return if worsening pain, fever, back pain, new symptoms, or recurrence.  
- Follow-up: phone/video or face-to-face if no improvement.  
- No immediate imaging or labs ordered; consider mid-stream urine (MSU) for culture if symptoms recur or persist.  

Consider:
- Pathology tests as above:  consider_pathology_or_not_recorded (MSU culture and pregnancy test suggested if no improvement)  
- EPC referral for allied health (10x visits/year):  consider_epc_or_not_recorded  
- Dental referral:  consider_dental_or_not_recorded  
- Optometry referral:  consider_optometry_or_not_recorded  
- Audiometry referral:  consider_audiometry_referral_or_not_recorded

- CTG registration (if not enrolled):  consider_ctg_or_not_recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: suprapubic pain, frequency, visible hematuria, minimal systemic features.  
2. Distal urolithiasis – Moderate likelihood: hematuria and abdominal discomfort but pain not colicky; frequency favors cystitis.  
3. Early appendicitis – Low-Medium likelihood: central pain and mild nausea but urinary findings unexplained.
